title: Gaussian lower-left quadrant probability
statement: Let $-1<\rho<1$ and $t\in\mathbb R$. If $\beta=1-\mathbb P(Z>t)$ for a standard normal random variable $Z$, then the probability that both coordinates of a centered bivariate standard normal pair with correlation $\rho$ are at most $t$ equals the probability that both coordinates are greater than the upper quantile corresponding to $\beta$.
